vignette: Leilani had always been drawn to helping others. As a parole officer, she worked tirelessly to support those reentering society after incarceration. But it was her previous role as a relief worker in a war zone that still lingered in her mind, haunting her every waking moment. The memories of the devastation and the people she couldn't save had left an indelible mark on her psyche. When she recalled the events of that fateful day, Leilani found herself pushing against the memories, trying to block them out before they became too vivid. She would catch glimpses of fragmented images – a child's face, a bombed-out building – but whenever she tried to recall more, her mind seemed to shut down. There were parts of the event that she simply couldn't remember, no matter how hard she tried. The more she pushed against these memories, the harder it became to deliberately recall what had happened. At times, seemingly innocuous things would trigger a flood of emotions: the taste of certain foods, reminiscent of the meager rations they'd eaten in the war zone; expressions of anger from others, even when calmly expressed – it all seemed to transport her back to those chaotic days. Leilani couldn't help but feel a sense of unease whenever she encountered reminders of victims – the faces, the stories, the desperation in their eyes. As time went on, these triggers began to affect Leilani's daily life as a parole officer. She found herself avoiding certain cases or clients that might bring up painful memories. Her colleagues noticed her growing withdrawal and began to wonder if she was okay. At home, Leilani became increasingly isolated, struggling to connect with her loved ones. Despite her best efforts, the memories continued to seep into her daily life. The taste of a particular spice would transport her back to the makeshift kitchen where they'd served meals to displaced families. A news report about another conflict zone would bring up images of the devastation she'd witnessed firsthand. Leilani began to feel like she was losing control, as if these memories were slowly consuming her. It was only when she found herself unable to sleep for weeks on end, plagued by nightmares and flashbacks, that Leilani realized she needed help. The weight of those memories had become too much to bear alone. She knew it wouldn't be easy, but with a deep breath, she reached out to seek the support she so desperately needed – hoping to finally break free from the grip of her past.
